message.content:
Review: The method is systematic and closely aligned with the research question. It separates pilot from confirmatory runs, randomizes run-level interventions, includes drive as a factor, and addresses blocking, carryover, baseline comparability, censoring, and multiple-window false-onset risk. Its measurement plan is substantially more precise than the supplied aggregate data allow: it specifies synchronized unit-level acquisition, spatial correlation fitting, subharmonic spectral analysis, phase coherence, and persistence. The analysis also distinguishes the randomized effect of coupling from the conditional mechanistic claim that correlation length mediates that effect, and appropriately limits generalization to the tested regime.

Feedback: Before preregistration, make the primary estimand and decision rule more explicit: identify the primary coupling contrast (including which levels and drive condition), define how onset and persistence contrasts will be summarized, and specify how multiplicity across those outcomes and factorial contrasts will be controlled. Clarify the relationship between the proposed sustained criterion in drive cycles and the time-windowed detection procedure, since consecutive-cycle persistence and overlapping spectral windows may not map directly onto one another. Also specify the exact correlation estimator and anisotropy summary, phase-coherence estimator, and the operational definition of “same operating regime.” The pilot can inform feasibility and variance, but keep confirmatory thresholds and analysis choices fixed independently of confirmatory outcomes. These refinements would improve reproducibility; they do not undermine the strong overall design.

Rating (1-5): 4
